evidence.excerpt: Walden Robotics release, Business Wire, 15 Jul 2026 (also Yahoo Finance, Bloomberg, Boston Globe, TechCrunch-tier coverage the same day): Walden Robotics launched out of stealth with $300M in seed funding at a $1.1B valuation, co-led by Toyota (Toyota Motor Corporation, Toyota Invention Partners and Toyota Ventures) and Deviation Capital; strategic investors Nvidia, Boeing, AE Ventures, Samsung Ventures, Prologis Ventures and CoreWeave Ventures; financial investors Calibrate Ventures, Colle Capital, Shine Capital, NextView Ventures, Squarepoint Capital, One Madison Group, KAS Venture Partners and Menlo Ventures, among others. Founded in January 2026 out of Toyota Research Institute by robotics and AI researchers from TRI, MIT, Stanford and Amazon; headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Since February its general-purpose robots (two arms and a sensor head on a wheeled or fixed base, no legs) have been doing useful work in production at a Toyota plant in North America, moving from first pilot to real work in under two months. The robots run on Large Behavior Models (LBMs), the model class the team helped pioneer, and learn new tasks through practice.

Boston Globe, 15 Jul 2026 ('Stealthy Toyota spinout gets one of Boston area's biggest robotics deals ever') and Bloomberg the same day: Russ Tedrake, co-founder and chief executive, is an MIT professor (the university's Toyota Professor of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science) who spent a decade at Toyota Research Institute, latterly as senior vice president of large behavior models, before spinning the company out of the lab in January 2026. Cambridge, Massachusetts.

The Robot Report, 15 Jul 2026, waldenrobotics.com/company and LinkedIn (search summaries, 15 Sep 2026): co-founder and Chief Technology Officer Ben Burchfiel; co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer Adrien Gaidon (led the ML organisation at Toyota Research Institute, adjunct professor at Stanford); Chief Product Officer Dave Johnson (Draper Labs, Dexai Robotics); founding head of hardware Andy Marchese (a decade at Amazon Robotics); head of software Joe Romano (Berkshire Grey, Kiva Systems). The company page lists CEO, CTO, COO, CPO, CSO, Principal Architect and Head of AI roles; no chief marketing officer, chief commercial officer or head of partnerships appears. The decision path is founders only.

DC Velocity, i-SCOOP and ASSEMBLY, Jul 2026 (search summaries): launch materials highlight machine tending, tool setting, parts kitting and assembly - loading and unloading car parts, cleaning machinery and kitting for assembly - with the North American Toyota factory deployment running shifts alongside human teams. Walden began working with customers across multiple industries at launch, with strategic partners in automotive, aerospace, semiconductors, electronics, logistics and life sciences.

haasf1team.com ('Inside the HQ: Exploring our US base'; 'United States'): the team's headquarters is in Kannapolis, North Carolina, with a European base in Banbury, Oxfordshire, that turns the cars around between races, and a design office in Maranello. Founder Gene Haas is the founder of Haas Automation, the largest CNC machine-tool builder in North America, and the team's CNC shop is central to operations on site in the US. Haas is the American privateer on the grid.

Toyota global newsroom, Oct 2024, haasf1team.com and ESPN, Dec 2025: Toyota Gazoo Racing and Haas agreed a multi-year technical partnership in October 2024 - vehicle development, data analysis, wind-tunnel testing and carbon-fibre parts, with a simulator installed at the Banbury base for 2026 - under the banner 'People, Product, Pipeline' (developing drivers, engineers and mechanics). From 2026 TGR replaced MoneyGram as title partner and the entry is TGR Haas F1 Team. TGR Europe's base is in Cologne.

Sponsor table (2026, active/joined) and team profiles: no robotics or humanoid brand on any of the eleven F1 rosters. ABB is the title partner of the Formula E championship since 2018 (the ABB FIA Formula E World Championship) and is a global robotics and automation group, which closes FE to a rival robotics brand. Siemens (industrial software and automation) is a partner of Oracle Red Bull Racing and Visa Cash App Racing Bulls. CoreWeave, a Walden investor, is a partner of Aston Martin Aramco F1 Team. Toyota Gazoo Racing is the title partner at Haas. Carmaker alignment on the 2026 grid: Cadillac (GM), Mercedes, Ferrari, Audi, Alpine (Renault), Aston Martin (Honda power from 2026), McLaren; Williams and Haas are the independents.

F1 Versus and SportBusiness Sponsorship (2026, REPORTED): the Toyota Gazoo Racing title at Haas is valued at $20-30M a year. 1440's $3-5M a year for an Official Robotics Partner entry is an ESTIMATE at partner tier, part-payable in robot deployments.

2026 F1 calendar (seeds/calendar_2026.json): round 19 United States GP (Austin), round 20 Mexico City GP, round 21 São Paulo GP, round 22 Las Vegas GP, round 23 Qatar GP, round 24 Abu Dhabi GP close the season in October-December. Teams close the following year's partner rosters in the fourth quarter; the winter build for the 2027 car runs December to February, which is when a factory-floor pilot can run without touching a race weekend.

brief.deck: Walden Robotics, the Toyota Research Institute spin-out whose wheeled, two-armed robots have worked a Toyota plant floor since February, came out of stealth on 15 July with a $300M seed at a $1.1B valuation, co-led by Toyota and Deviation Capital, with Nvidia, Boeing and Samsung Ventures behind it.
brief.the_case_p1: The company was founded in January 2026 out of Toyota Research Institute by Russ Tedrake, the MIT professor who ran TRI's large-behavior-model work. Its robots have two arms and a sensor head on a wheeled base, no legs, and run on Large Behavior Models that learn a task through practice. At a Toyota plant in North America they went from first pilot to production in under two months and now run shifts alongside human teams: machine tending, tool setting, parts kitting, loading and unloading. Strategic partners span automotive, aerospace, semiconductors, electronics and logistics.
brief.the_case_p2: No robotics brand sits on the 2026 F1 grid, and the one team titled by Walden's lead investor runs its own CNC shop: Haas is owned by Gene Haas, founder of Haas Automation, the largest CNC machine-tool builder in North America. Machine tending is the task Walden's robots already do at Toyota. The lane is open and the workstream is literal.

why_now.label: A deployment company, not a lab
why_now.text: The company spun out of Toyota Research Institute in January 2026 and had robots doing production work at a Toyota plant in North America by February, moving from first pilot to real work in under two months. Its own line is that the hard problem in robotics is now deployment, not research. A company selling deployments to manufacturers needs a stage where manufacturers, engineers and recruits are watching, and a Formula 1 factory is one.

## Decision path

Russ Tedrake (co-founder and Chief Executive Officer) is the decision-maker: the company page lists CEO, CTO, COO, CPO, CSO, Principal Architect and Head of AI roles and no marketing, commercial or partnerships title; the brief says so. Path: Adrien Gaidon (co-founder and Chief Strategy Officer — the partnership owner by title), Ben Burchfiel (co-founder and Chief Technology Officer — technical counterpart), Dave Johnson (Chief Product Officer). The COO is listed as a role on the company page; the name was not confirmed from a source the desk could reach and is not given.

## Leadership ties

Tedrake, Burchfiel, Gaidon, Johnson, Marchese, Romano: **none found** in F1 or Formula E after checking. Toyota Research Institute is Toyota's research arm, not Toyota Gazoo Racing; the tie is corporate, through the investor, and the brief says so.

## Team choice

TGR Haas F1 Team on the investor link and grid occupancy: the only team titled by Walden's lead investor, an owner whose company builds CNC machines, and no robotics brand on any F1 roster. Formula E is closed by ABB's title. Williams is the named fallback (independent, open lane, no Toyota link). Haas is the twelfth F1 case pointed at the team; chosen on the Toyota tie and the CNC shop, not habit.
